title: WESTERN HEAT / BRAINS 25
dek: Three kinds of football pressure. One Saturday scoreboard for brains.
body:
Arizona State is the best football proposition today. Colorado is the most watched construction site. Wyoming carries the most meaning per win. That is the opening board in Western Heat: an editorial index of pressure, leverage, and what a season does to the meaning of a university.

ASU uses football to compress a distributed university and sprawling Valley into one shared civic clock. Colorado uses football to open a national aperture, then has to prove the attention can become development and continuity. Wyoming uses football as a state commons for the state’s only four-year public university. The temperatures are disclosed PointCast judgments. Records, weather, attendance, research, and money remain linked to their sources.

The second side is Brains 25, a proposed sports desk for American research that refuses to pretend every number is the same kind of score. The Power 25 reproduces NSF/NCSES FY2024 research expenditure: the size of the machine, not the quality of discovery. The Saturday Scoreboard records public proof from NASA and Department of Energy student competitions, missions, prototypes, and systems that had to work outside the lab.

Today’s category is systems under pressure. Virginia’s Lunabotics team takes the first spot after a wheel detached and the machine kept moving. Missouri S&T repeated as University Rover Challenge champion. MIT went first and second in NASA RASC-AL. USC won the Marine Energy Collegiate Competition. South Dakota State won NASA’s Gateways to Blue Skies. These are unlike competitions and remain separate results; the desk remembers them together without inventing a false national championship.

Every future entry gets four lines—case, doubt, next proof, movement—and five visible dials: scale, proof, student agency, public value, and openness. The dream is not ESPN for science. It is a publication that remembers what the score meant.
